RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

Member: Harper Hayes, Member ID W668248955
Service: Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-15
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-11

Dear Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-15 (Reference No. POC-E8E7B452F1-10979). This appeal is being submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in that notice.

**Stated reason for denial**

The notice states that the request was denied because "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I dispute this determination. As detailed below, the clinical record documents an extensive, well-documented, and unsuccessful course of conservative treatment, together with objective imaging findings that support surgical repair without further delay.

**Applicable plan criteria**

Tufts Health Plan's musculoskeletal surgery (hip/knee/shoulder) prior authorization program is administered by its vendor, Evolent (formerly National Imaging Associates). The publicly available Evolent Clinical Guideline for Shoulder Arthroscopy (Guideline No. Evolent_CG_1770) states, regarding non-operative management for shoulder conditions generally:

"Non-operative management, when required, will be specified within the clinical indications below and may include one or more of the following: Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program; Rest or activity modification; Application of heat or ice; Minimum of 4 weeks of oral NSAIDs (if not medically contraindicated); Single injection of corticosteroid and local anesthetic into subacromial, intra-articular space, or bicipital groove."

The same guideline states, specifically as to rotator cuff repair:

"Surgical treatment of a rotator cuff tear (RCT) should only be performed when there is a clinical correlation of symptoms, clinical exam findings, imaging, and failed non-operative management (where required)."

The guideline also directs that clinical notes should address "Symptom onset, duration, and severity; Loss of function and/or limitations; Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable)."

I was not able to obtain the specific subsection of this guideline that applies to a medium-sized (1–3 cm), full-thickness supraspinatus tear with fatty atrophy — the category that appears to match this member's diagnosis — because that portion of the document was not accessible to me. I am therefore not quoting or assuming any size-specific duration requirement beyond what is set out above, and I respectfully request that Tufts Health Plan/Evolent identify, in writing, the exact section and specific criterion of Guideline Evolent_CG_1770 (or any other medical necessity guideline actually applied) that it contends was not met, so that the record can be directly addressed.

**How the clinical record satisfies the general conservative-treatment requirements quoted above**

1. **Duration and severity of symptoms:** Ms. Hayes has experienced 12 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest.

2. **Physical therapy:** Ms. Hayes completed a supervised course of physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics — 24 visits over 8 weeks, from 2026-05-08 to 2026-07-03 — as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This satisfies the "physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program" element identified in the guideline language quoted above.

3. **Oral NSAIDs:** Ms. Hayes was treated with NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, well in excess of the "minimum of 4 weeks of oral NSAIDs" referenced in the guideline.

4. **Corticosteroid injection:** Ms. Hayes received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-13, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned — satisfying the "single injection of corticosteroid and local anesthetic" element referenced in the guideline, with a documented poor/transient response.

5. **Functional limitation:** Ms. Hayes cannot lift her arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side, documenting the "loss of function and/or limitations" the guideline asks providers to address.

6. **Objective examination findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain are documented, satisfying the guideline's requirement of "clinical correlation of individual's subjective complaints with objective exam findings."

7. **Imaging findings:** MRI of the shoulder dated 2026-07-09 confirms a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. This is the objective imaging correlation called for in the guideline language quoted above ("clinical correlation of symptoms, clinical exam findings, imaging, and failed non-operative management").

8. **Surgical readiness / absence of contraindications:** The record documents no active local or systemic infection and no untreated substance use — consistent with the general requirement that the individual "does not have an active local or systemic infection" and "does not have active, untreated drug dependency." Ms. Hayes's BMI is 29, and she is a non-smoker.

In my own words, and not as a quotation from any plan document: it is also clinically relevant that the presence of grade 2 fatty atrophy on the July 2026 MRI is a recognized indicator that further delay in repair may reduce the likelihood of a successful surgical outcome. I ask that the reviewing clinician take this into account when weighing whether additional non-operative treatment would be appropriate before surgery.

**Conclusion and request**

Taken together, the record documents 8 weeks (24 visits) of supervised physical therapy, 6 months of NSAID therapy, and a corticosteroid injection with only transient benefit, alongside objective exam and imaging findings and significant functional limitation. This satisfies every element of conservative management described in the Evolent Shoulder Arthroscopy guideline language quoted above. I therefore request that Tufts Health Plan reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 29827 (arthroscopic rotator cuff repair) as requested by Dr. Marchetti.

If any additional documentation is needed, or if the plan is applying size-specific criteria not quoted above, please identify the specific criterion and provide a copy of the applicable guideline so that the treating surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, and I can respond directly to it.

Enclosed with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-08 to 2026-07-03, 24 visits)
- Documentation of NSAID trial (6 months)
- Corticosteroid injection record (2026-05-13) and follow-up notes
- MRI report dated 2026-07-09
- Office visit/examination notes documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Marchetti [if available]
- [Any additional records the provider wishes to include]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing within 48 hours, as described in Tufts Health Plan's member appeal procedures, and provide the name, address, and telephone number of the person coordinating review of this appeal.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Harper Hayes
